extraction_warnings: No canonical study_name, subject_id, or sample_id values are provided in the text; these were marked not_reported.
pmid value was taken from the externally supplied paper_id, not from in-text content.

Sequencing platform is only explicitly named (Illumina HiSeq) for the 16S sequencing of transplanted-mouse fecal samples; the main human shotgun metagenomic sequencing is described only generically as 'Illumina platform'.
Age, sex ratio, and additional clinical parameters are referenced as being in Additional file 1: Table S1, which was not included in the provided text, so numeric values could not be extracted.
The enum field 'control' role was inferred from group definitions (healthy controls vs. pHTN/HTN patients) rather than an explicit case/control statement using those exact allowed-value terms.
Batch 1 subgroups ['control', 'pre-hypertension', 'hypertension'] differ from batch 0 ['control', 'pHTN', 'HTN']; kept batch 0.

This paper is a human hypertension gut microbiome study (not a cancer, neonatal, twin, or reproductive-health cohort); many schema fields (zygosity, tumor staging, neonatal, obgyn, HLA) are not applicable and were marked not_reported.
Age, BMI, and gender were mentioned only as covariates without specific numeric values reported in the accessible text (details likely in Additional file 1: Table S1, not provided).
Smoker and antibiotics_current_use fields were inferred from exclusion criteria rather than directly stated participant status; treat with caution.
FMT donor/recipient information exists but recipients were germ-free mice, not human participants, limiting applicability of fmt_role/fmt_id fields to human subject-level metadata.

Disease subgroup values (control/pre-hypertension/hypertension) were extracted from Methods — Study cohort and patient characteristics using blood pressure thresholds, not standard disease ontology terms verbatim.

biomarker_name/unit/value fields were populated using the BP classification thresholds (SBP/DBP) that define control/pHTN/HTN groups, since no other clearly labeled 'biomarker' with paired name/unit/value triplets was reported at study or sample level.

feces_phenotype_value could not be mapped to a specific reported value despite extensive microbiome diversity/composition data being present; consider manual review of Figures 1-3 and Additional files for possible relevant values.
host_species was inferred as Homo sapiens for the main cohort; the study also includes a mouse (Mus musculus) FMT experiment, which is not separately represented in the schema.

Overall granularity was set to subgroup_level because the most schema-relevant quantitative data (BP thresholds) differ by control/pHTN/HTN subgroup; many other results (microbiome diversity, metabolomics) are also subgroup-stratified but not directly mapped to schema fields.
